Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the latency looked great in the flow you showed. We're planning a 48-hour overnight soak next week to validate steady-state throughput and tail-latency under our real traffic patterns. The soak runs 11pm–7am PST and will spike a few times overnight.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood provision a small promotional credit/stipend for that window (we estimate ~140k tokens total)?
- Any configuration suggestions to avoid cold-starts impacting tail latency (we'll stick with the model you recommended but will run long sequences)?

I've attached a short plan and traffic export. If you want, Anya (cc) will share the Grafana tokens so you can see the ramp schedule.

Appreciate it — this run is a gating item for our internal POC sign-off.

—Marco

Hi all —

Short guidance for the overnight soak:
- Pre-warm: create a 30-min pre-warm window starting 30 minutes before first spike. Use pinned instances if you can (we can do that on hosted by reserving warm slots).
- Batch config: set max_batch_latency to 15ms and token_batch_size to 64 for the expected request distribution.
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for repeated prompts (if your traffic has common prefixes this will reduce tail latencies).
- Monitoring: include our tracing header (x-rdw-trace) so our Debug team can correlate traces if you hit tail spikes.

I'll put a short config snippet in the Drive link and can join a 15-min call tomorrow if useful.

—Logan (SRE)
